title: castilleja affinis subsp. litoralis
intro: Castilleja affinis subsp. litoralis, commonly known as Indian paintbrush, is a flowering plant species native to the coastal regions of the Pacific Northwest in North America. The plant is known for its unique, reddish-orange to red flowers that resemble a paintbrush. Castilleja affinis subsp. litoralis has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, including its potential to aid in the treatment of various health issues such as respiratory problems, fever, and infections due to its health benefits of being an expectorant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial agent. The bioactive constituents of Castilleja affinis subsp. litoralis include alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions of soothing coughs, reducing inflammation, and preventing the growth of microorganisms.
